newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Caracas stocks end higher as blue chips rebound.
newsitem.headline: Caracas stocks end higher as blue chips rebound.

text.p: Caracas stocks closed slightly higher Friday as investors hunted for bargains among blue chips, traders said.
"The market as a whole gained on the strength of specific trades in selected stocks," said one broker.
Traders singled out strong trading in steel company Sivensa, which rose 9.25 bolivars to end at 320.

The bolsa's index edged 0.28 percent ahead to close at 5,838.73, as 16 shares fell, 16 rose and six were unchanged. A total of 17.3 million shares, worth 2.8 billion bolivars ($6 million), changed hands.

"The market's been thin all week and will continue to be so until the CANTV issue is over," said Vencred broker Geronimo Paolini, referring to the government's sale of most of its stake in the Venezuelan telephone company.

With activity expected to pick up after November 19, when the CANTV book-building period ends, traders identified foods producer Mavesa Electricidad de Caracas and Sivensa as strong candidates to lead any rally.
"They could zoom ahead," said Interacciones broker Freddy Zambrano.
